subtype: Approach: uses waiting as a way to avoid a needed decision [Pitfall]
passage:
In the Class 12 counselling room, Aparna slid the two course forms across the desk. "The last date is the fifteenth. Have you picked?"

Santosh shrugged. "I'll sleep on it."

A week later he said it again, and the week after that. Each time Aparna asked what he had found out, he said, "Nothing new, I'm still thinking." He had not opened either college website or asked a senior about the hostel. On the sixteenth he came in with the forms still unsigned and read the notice on the board.

"It closed yesterday." He stared at the paper. "I thought more time would just make it clear."

Aparna pulled a chair up beside him and asked what he wanted to do about it now.

qa.q: On which date had the forms closed?
qa.a: The forms closed on the fifteenth, the day before Santosh read the notice.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling as he read the notice on the board?
qa.a: Santosh was shocked and probably regretful, staring at the paper after hoping that more time would make things clear.

qa.q: What could Santosh have done with those weeks instead of only waiting?
qa.a: Santosh could have set a date to decide, opened the college websites and asked a senior about the hostel, so there were new facts to think about.

qa.q: How might Aparna have felt each time Santosh said he would sleep on it?
qa.a: Aparna may have felt concerned and a little helpless, seeing nothing new gathered while the last date came closer.

grounding: Shows a student using 'sleeping on it' with no end date and gathering nothing, so a deadline passes.

subtype: Approach: uses waiting as a way to avoid a needed decision [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Naveen,
You asked why I'm not joining the design college with you this August. I owe you the true answer.
In January I had two options: design in Ahmedabad or the engineering seat here in Nagpur. I told everyone, including you, "I'll sleep on it." And I did. For weeks.
But sleeping on it meant nothing new. I didn't visit either college. I didn't call any seniors. I didn't ask my parents about fees. I just kept waiting for the answer to appear one morning.
The design application closed on 28 February. I noticed on 3 March.
So the choice got made anyway, by the calendar. I'm in engineering by default, not by decision.
Next time I say I'll sleep on something, ask me what date I'm deciding by.
Farhan

qa.q: When did Farhan notice the design application had closed?
How does Farhan seem to feel about the outcome?
qa.a: Farhan seems regretful and a bit ashamed, being in engineering by default rather than by choice.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Farhan waited?
qa.a: Set a decision date before the deadline and gather something new each week, like calling a senior or visiting a college, so waiting leads somewhere.

qa.q: How might Naveen feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Naveen may feel sad to lose a friend at college and a bit sorry that Farhan's waiting cost the chance.

grounding: It shows a student who keeps saying they will sleep on a college choice for weeks, gathering nothing new until the deadline passes.

subtype: Approach: uses waiting as a way to avoid a needed decision [Pitfall]
passage:
Manoj, you keep saying you'll think about the internship offer. Let Uday tell you what happened to me last year, so you don't repeat it.
I had a choice between a college in Pune and one in Bhopal for my master's. Both had given me a seat. I told my family, "Let me sleep on it." Everyone respected that.
Then I slept on it for five weeks. I didn't call anyone from either college. I didn't compare the courses properly. I didn't even look at hostel fees. I kept thinking that one morning I'd just wake up knowing.
The Pune fee deadline was a Friday. I was still "sleeping on it" that Friday. By Monday the seat had gone to the waiting list.
So I'm in Bhopal. It's fine, honestly. But I didn't choose it. I just waited until only one door was open.
Sleeping on something only works if you're doing something while you're awake.

qa.q: How many weeks did Uday sleep on the choice?
qa.a: Uday slept on it for five weeks.

qa.q: How does Uday feel looking back?
qa.a: Uday feels regretful, not unhappy with Bhopal but uneasy about never actually choosing it.

qa.q: What else could Uday have done during those five weeks, and why?
qa.a: Uday could have set a date before the Pune deadline and called students from both colleges, so the waiting brought in new facts.

qa.q: How might Manoj be affected by hearing this story?
qa.a: Manoj may feel a push to set a deadline for the internship decision instead of waiting for the answer to appear.

grounding: It shows a student who keeps sleeping on a college choice for weeks without gathering anything new, until a deadline passes and the choice is made by default.
